column1: # Consumer Credit Matters — Auto Loan ABS — Recovery on Defaulted Loans
# Source: SEC Form ABS-EE loan-level filings of the public auto-loan shelves
column2: checked against their monthly servicer reports (SEC Form 10-D)

column1: # Definition: Cash collected on loans that defaulted in four consecutive quarters
column2: within 12 (or 6) months of default and net of repossession and sale costs
column3: over the balance owed the month before default; https://data.consumercreditmatters.com/abs/methodology.html#recoveries

column1: # Note: Shelves withheld for data quality are not in the file; the methodology page lists them and why.
# Columns: shelf = the shelf's ticker (ALL = every loan shelf pooled; ALL-LEASE = every lease shelf pooled); shelf_name = the issuer; window_end = last month of the four default quarters
column2: YYYY-MM; defaults_window = the four default quarters; horizon_months = months after default the cash is counted (12; 6 = the early read); recovery_rate = recovered cash / balance at default; loss_severity = 1 - recovery_rate; margin_95 = 95% margin of the rate (same units; applies to severity too); defaulted_loans = loans in the cohort; low_precision = true where the margin is wider than 3 percentage points; early_read = true for 6-month windows not yet 12 months past default
